**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), § 6(a) [p0032].**

**The problem.** Two defects, one in each direction:

1. *Missing customer convenience right.* § 2 makes the Agreement evergreen ("shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), yet § 6(a) allows convenience termination only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." Since all Services are delivered task-by-task under SOWs (§ 1(a)), we are locked in for the life of every open SOW — with no ceiling on SOW duration. Our only mid-engagement exit is material breach under § 6(b).
2. *Vendor may walk away on short notice.* Contractor's fifteen (15) days is well below the 90-day walk-away floor.

**The redline (validated, ok:true).** Single-paragraph edit to § 6(a): adds our 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, expressly without penalty, early-termination charge or acceleration, with refund of prepaid fees; and reassigns the existing "no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding" gate to Contractor alone at 90 days' notice.

**Points worth noting for negotiation.** Fees are time-and-materials (§ 3(a)), so the refund limb will rarely bite — it is cheap for Contractor to concede and protects us against any prepaid or milestone SOW. § 6(b) already preserves Contractor's payment for Services rendered through the termination date, so no fee-cap language was needed. Fallback if Contractor pushes back: 60 days' notice for us, holding Contractor at 90 days end-of-term only.
